title: What is known about 1RB0LD_1RC1RE_1LA0LD_1LB1LC_0RA1RF_1RA---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LD_1RC1RE_1LA0LD_1LB1LC_0RA1RF_1RA---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The run is described exactly (checked against direct simulation) by an item-level counter whose sweeps are a binary carry chain on the parities of the block lengths. The item simulator ran 5·1010 sweeps (4.3·1021 machine steps) without meeting a sweep it does not model; a halt needs one particular small pattern in the slowly changing tail of the list. Lean proves the main sweep rules for all block lengths and that the halting pattern does halt.

claims.title: Sweeps for all lengths
claims.text: From a sweep start D> 0 0 (10)^n0 0 …: item 0 even decrements item 1 (x_at_1); item 0 even with item 1 empty resets (reset_at_1); item 0 odd and item 1 even passes to item 2 (y_x_at_2); two odd items pass to item 3 (yy_x_at_3), each for all lengths and any tape further right.

claims.title: Where a halt comes from
claims.text: A sweep whose signal passes an odd item 0 and meets an even item with separator 1, followed by an empty item with separator 1 and a further 1, halts (F reads a 1).

claims.title: The item model is exact
claims.text: The parity-signal rule, the four special sweeps (reset, merge, end-decrement, end-reset) and their exact step counts agree with cell-by-cell sweeps on 37,000 random item lists and with every sweep start of a direct run from blank tape (1,201 sweeps, 3·10<sup>6</sup> steps; the C version also matches all 3,494 sweep starts of the first 3·10<sup>7</sup> steps).

claims.title: No halt in 4.3·10<sup>21</sup> steps
claims.text: The C item simulator ran 5·10<sup>10</sup> sweeps (4.3·10<sup>21</sup> steps) and every sweep was one it models, so no halt occurred; the list then had 36 items.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: A counter that slowly eats its tail
claims.text: Item k is decremented about once every 2<sup>k</sup> sweeps, so the small items left at the far end from the first few hundred steps change only every 2<sup>30</sup> sweeps or so. A halt needs a specific small pattern there; nothing seen so far rules it out or makes it likely.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. A proof of non-halting would need an invariant of the item lists that is closed under the sweep rules and excludes the unmodelled sweeps, and a Lean proof of the general sweep (any depth).

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine builds an odometer out of blocks of 1 0 1 0 …: every sweep of the head carries a signal to the right that skips blocks of odd length and shortens the block after the first even one, like the carry of a binary counter. We have an exact description of every sweep, and ran it far beyond direct simulation, but the far end of the tape keeps a few small blocks from its first moments, and whether they ever line up into the one pattern that halts is unknown.

facts.text: No halt: 5·10<sup>10</sup> sweeps of the exact item model.
Proved in Lean for all block lengths, and the halting pattern.
A halt needs a small pattern in the slowly-changing far end.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.477). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 81,747 cells (60,778 left of the start, 56 right), with a density of 1s of 0.551.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: What the tape is made of
html: Look at the tape each time the head, in state D, reaches a new cell on the left: it is a list of items, each a block of alternating cells (1 0)^n followed by one separator cell, 0 or 1:
D> 0 (10)^n0 s0 (10)^n1 s1 … (10)^nk sk with s0 = 0 and sk = 1

Write the list as pairs (n, s). After the first few hundred steps there are 10 to 35 items, most with separator 0; the first items are long (billions of pairs after 1010 sweeps), the last few are short leftovers from the start of the run.

sections.heading: One sweep is a carry
html: The head runs right, turning each block it crosses into solid 1s, and back left, turning them back. What it changes is decided by a signal it carries, set by parities. Leaving item 0 the signal is X (act) if n0 is even and Y (pass) if it is odd. A Y crossing an item with separator 0 leaves it alone and becomes X if that item's length is even, Y if odd. An X shortens the item it reaches by one pair and the sweep ends. Every sweep also adds 3 pairs to item 0, which flips its parity.

Read the parities bi = ni mod 2 as binary digits: the sweep skips the run of 1-digits at the front and shortens the item just after the first 0-digit, exactly where the carry of a binary counter would stop. So item k is touched about once every 2k sweeps. Items with separator 1 (fresh ones) are handled slightly differently: a Y passing one sets its separator to 0, taking a pair from the next item if its length was even.
The step count of a sweep that acts on item d is exactly 12 + 3d + 3·Σj<d(2nj+1), plus 2 or 4 for each separator-1 item crossed.

sections.heading: When an item runs out
html: <table class="tbl"><thead><tr><th>sweep</th><th>when</th><th>what happens</th></tr></thead><tbody>
resetX reaches an empty item (0, 0)everything before it shifts one place right with separator 1, a new item (2, 0) appears in front, the item before the empty one gains 1, the empty one disappears
mergeX reaches an empty (0, 1) inside the list(p, 0) (0, 1) (m, s) becomes (p + m, s)
end decrementX reaches an empty (0, 1) at the end(p, 0) (0, 1) becomes (p − 1, 1): the tape's right end moves left
end resetY reaches the last item (m, 1)like a reset of the whole list; the last item becomes (m + 2, 1), or (m + 1, 1) (1, 1) if m is even

So the list behaves like an odometer whose digits have unbounded size: the front item counts sweeps, an exhausted item pushes the front item into the list, and the list grows by one item now and then (about logarithmically).

sections.heading: Where it could halt
html: The halting transition is F reading 1. It is reached when a Y signal meets an even item with separator 1 whose successor is an empty item with separator 1 followed by a 1 (halt_case). More generally, any sweep outside the rules above is suspect; the item simulator stops on such a sweep, and none has occurred in 5·1010 sweeps. Separator-1 items created by resets are odd and are turned into separator-0 items by the next passes, so small separator-1 items mostly live at the far end: leftovers like (175, 1) (69, 1) (7, 1) (1, 1) that the carry reaches only once every 230 sweeps or so, and that the end resets keep feeding with new (1, 1) items. Whether they ever form the halting pattern is the open question.

sections.heading: What is proved
html: In Lean (kernel), for all block lengths: the sweeps that act on items 1, 2 and 3 and the reset at item 1 (lean/Rules.lean), and that the halting pattern halts (lean/Halt.lean). The general sweep for any depth, and an invariant of the item lists that would exclude the halting pattern forever, are not proved; the item model is a trusted computation checked against direct simulation.

summary: The tape is a list of blocks (10)^n; each sweep sends a signal right that passes blocks of odd length and decrements the block after the first even one (a binary carry chain on the parities), the front block grows by 3, and an emptied block makes the list shift; exact item model run for 5e10 sweeps with no halt.
